identification.name: H13 Tool Steel (Hardened + Tempered)
identification.common_form_notes: Supplied in the soft-annealed condition (max 207–241 HB) as round bar, flat bar, and plate from tool steel stockholders. The tool maker performs the hardening heat treatment. Premium ESR (electroslag-remelted) grades — Uddeholm ORVAR Supreme, Bohler W302 Superior — offer improved cleanliness and isotropic toughness. Also available as gas-atomised powder for DMLS/SLM conformal-cooled tooling.
identification.notes: H13 is a hot-work chromium tool steel (AISI H13, UNS T20813, DIN 1.2344, EN X40CrMoV5-1). Properties are for the standard die casting die working condition: austenitised at 1010°C (1850°F) for 15–40 min, high-pressure gas or oil quenched, then double-tempered 2 × 2 h at ~580°C to achieve ~44–46 HRC. Data shown (yield 1280 MPa, UTS 1420 MPa, HRC 45) are for Uddeholm ORVAR Supreme premium ESR-grade H13; standard H13 achieves comparable values. Strength and hardness are strongly tempering-temperature-dependent: 540°C temper → ~50 HRC (maximum strength), 620°C → ~42 HRC (optimised thermal fatigue resistance). H13 exhibits a secondary hardening peak at ~500–510°C due to Mo/V carbide precipitation — this range is avoided as it produces peak hardness with poor toughness; NADCA recommended tempering range for die casting dies is 540–620°C. Hot hardness is H13's defining advantage over cold-work tool steels: useful hardness is retained to ~600°C, where D2 (cold-work) would be completely overtempered. In metal AM (DMLS/SLM/LPBF), H13 is well established: preheating the substrate to ≥200°C eliminates thermal cracking and achieves >99.9% relative density; as-built hardness is ~50 HRC; conformal cooling channel tooling is the primary industrial driver, yielding significant cycle time and part quality improvements over conventionally drilled cooling circuits. Welding requires pre-heat (250–350°C) and post-weld temper; generally used for repair only. HV 446 is converted from HRC 45 via ASTM E140. Shear strength derived from von Mises criterion: UTS/√3 = 1420/√3 ≈ 820 MPa. Thermal diffusivity derived from k, ρ, Cp for the hardened condition.

typical_usage: Die casting dies for aluminium, magnesium, and zinc; hot extrusion dies, liners, and mandrels; hot forging dies; injection mould cavities for engineering polymers; hot shear blades and trimmer dies; AM-built conformal-cooled die inserts and mould cores.
